title: Light and Heavy: luc, lev and grav
short: luc means light (brightness), lev means light (not heavy) and grav means heavy.
trouble: Two different "lights": luc is about brightness (lucid), lev about weight (levity, alleviate).

blocks.html: English uses “light” for two different ideas, and Latin had a root for each. luc (also lum) is light you see: to illuminate is to light up. lev is light you lift, the opposite of heavy: a lever lifts, and to elevate is to raise. And the opposite of lev is grav, “heavy”: gravity pulls heavy things down.

blocks.html: The luc words are about making things clear, as if a light were turned on: lucid writing is clear, and to elucidate is to bring out into the light. The lev and grav words are about weight: to alleviate is to make a burden lighter, and to aggravate is to make it heavier.

blocks.title: Use the parts
blocks.q: At the serious ceremony, the clown’s levity seemed out of place. What does levity mean?
steps: Take it apart: lev (light, not heavy) + -ity (the quality of).
Literally: “lightness.” Here it means a light, joking manner.
The sentence fits: joking at a serious event. Its opposite is gravity (seriousness).
blocks.a: Lightness of manner, especially at a serious time.

blocks.name: vo-word

entry.ex: Ada gave a {lucid} explanation of how rainbows form.
entry.ctx: The instruction booklet was a jumble of tiny print, but Grandpa’s note was {lucid}: three short steps, each with a simple drawing.
entry.etym: From Latin lucidus, “bright, clear,” from lux (light).

mn.text: Lucy’s map is so clear that anyone can follow it: one big arrow, three landmarks and an X. Her map is {lucid}.

blocks.name: vo-word

entry.def: lightness of mood or humor, especially at a serious time
entry.ex: A little {levity} helped the nervous players relax before the final game.
entry.ctx: The ceremony was solemn, and the principal frowned at any {levity}; even a giggle from the back row earned a stern look.

roots.means: the state or quality of being

entry.etym: From Latin levitas, “lightness,” from levis (light in weight).
entry.note: Levity can be welcome (it eases a tense room) or unwelcome (it seems disrespectful); the sentence tells you which.

mn.cue: LEV = LIGHT: a joke that LEVitates
mn.text: The long meeting feels heavy until Dev’s joke floats up like a balloon and lifts everyone’s mood: a moment of {levity}.

scene.alt: In an office meeting, a young man’s joke floats up like a balloon and his coworkers laugh.

blocks.cap: A word from the list: levity.

blocks.html: Confusing the two “lights.” luc is about brightness (lucid, elucidate: clear, made clear). lev is about weight (levity, alleviate: lightness, making lighter). Lucid writing is clear, not lightweight.
